posts.title: How often should a visit be booked?
posts.excerpt: A house with one new sighting is a different job from a kitchen that serves every night.
paragraphs: A single call-out is enough for many homes. Something has shown up, we find where it is living, treat that, and come back once to see if it has stopped.

A restaurant, hotel, or shared building is different. Food, waste, and deliveries keep arriving, so pests keep testing the same doors. Those sites do better on a standing gap: monthly, or whatever the building actually needs after the first inspection.
Cleaning every day does not close a drain, a gap behind a fridge, or a bin store that stays wet. The schedule is there to catch the next attempt early, not because the last treatment failed.
If you are unsure which you need, say what you have seen and what the building is. We will tell you whether one visit is the right start.

posts.title: What to plan when children are in the house
posts.excerpt: Most rooms do not need to be emptied for the whole day. You should still know which ones to keep clear.
paragraphs: The first question we ask is who sleeps and eats in the rooms we are treating. Children, and anyone who crawls on the floor, change how we set the visit up.
Before we start you will hear which rooms to stay out of, what to put away, and when those rooms can be used again. Food, bottles, and pet bowls come off the surfaces we will work on.

For a light cockroach or ant job, the household can often stay home and simply avoid the kitchen for a stated time. A heavy bed-bug job is different: that bedroom should be empty while we work, and bedding is dealt with first.
If you are pregnant, or a child has a breathing condition, say so when you book. We will plan the rooms around that.

posts.title: Disinfecting a home or an office
posts.excerpt: A surface treatment is for the rooms you can leave empty for a short time. It is not a substitute for cleaning.
paragraphs: Disinfection is a separate booking from pest treatment. It is for surfaces in a home, office, clinic, or hotel room that need a reset after illness, a deep clean, or a pest job.

We treat the surfaces we can reach: handles, desks, switches, and the fittings in the rooms on the list. A fine spray gets into gaps that a cloth misses. It does not replace wiping grease off a kitchen line.
You will be told which rooms to leave, and for how long, before anyone goes back in. Electronics, open food, and papers should be covered or moved.
Book it on its own, or add it to a pest visit when the same rooms need both.

posts.title: What a cockroach problem leaves behind
posts.excerpt: You may not see an insect in daylight. The cupboard often shows the problem first.
paragraphs: Cockroaches rest in dark gaps and come out to feed. By the time one crosses the floor at night, there are usually more in the void behind the appliances.
Look for dark specks in a drawer, smear marks along a kickboard, and a musty smell when a cupboard has been shut. Egg cases and shed skins mean they have been there long enough to breed.
Wiping the worktop removes what you can see. It does not reach the harbourage. That is the part the visit is for.
Empty the cupboard under the sink before we arrive if you can. The job is faster, and we can see the pipes.

posts.title: Spotting bed bugs before they spread
posts.excerpt: The sooner a guest room or bedroom is checked, the fewer pieces of furniture are involved.
paragraphs: Bed bugs stay near the sleeper. Early on, that means one bed. Left alone, they move to the next bed, the sofa, and the luggage rack.
Check the piping of the mattress and the joints of the headboard. Dark spots, shed skins, and specks on the sheet are the usual signs. Bites alone are not proof.
Do not move the mattress into another room to “air it”. That is how a second room gets involved. Bag the linen and tell us which room it came from.
In a hotel, take the room out of service and book the visit for after checkout. We will say whether the rooms on either side need a look as well.

posts.title: Why a kitchen does better on a schedule
posts.excerpt: A busy pass produces scraps, warmth, and a bin that is never empty for long.
paragraphs: One treatment can knock a kitchen problem back. It cannot change the fact that food and waste return the next day. Drains, the hot line, and the delivery door stay attractive.
A standing visit catches droppings, a new trail, or a failed door seal between services, while it is still small. The gap depends on the site. A small café is not a hotel production kitchen.
We book the round after closing and leave a note of what was found. The morning team should be able to open without a surprise.
If you only want a call-out because something showed up this week, that is still the right first step. The schedule is the conversation after we have seen the kitchen.
